jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

Provides, protects, and defends enterprise information services to approximately 45,000 Army, joint and DoD customers across the European theater on a 24 x 7 x 365 days per year basis on classified, unclassified, and coalition networks.

About The Role

Join a high-impact team supporting critical regulatory reporting initiatives for the U.S. derivatives markets.

We are looking to add a Data Analyst
to the team. In this role, you'll help define data standards, ensure the quality and integrity of market data, collaborate with industry stakeholders, and contribute to the oversight of both traditional derivatives and emerging prediction markets. If you have expertise in capital markets, data analysis, SQL, AWS, and regulatory reporting, we'd love to hear from you. Must be local the DMV area or Chicago, IL area.

What will you do:

Conduct analysis and develop reporting requirements to define data standards specifications, schemas, and validation rules for CFTC regulatory reporting obligations
Develop technical guidance, data-mapping documentation, FIXML examples, and updated guidebooks that incorporate schema changes and new validations.
Support DCMs, SEFs, and DCOs by answering data-submission questions and maintaining clear, up-to-date reference materials.
Perform detailed analysis of exchange-submitted data - including checks for duplicates, missing fields, and other errors, and cross-dataset mismatches, and conduct multi-platform comparisons in SQL Server and Redshift to identify and document gaps or anomalies. Additionally, support troubleshooting of UAT and production issues for large-volume inbound datasets.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders at CFTC including DMO, DCR, Enforcement, and the Division of Data and with external market participants to review and approve data standards specifications.
Participate in industry calls, regulatory working groups, validation meetings, while supporting onboarding of new DCM/SEF applicants by evaluating submissions, aligning them with CFTC requirements, and documenting necessary updates.
Support data loading & processing team in testing and trouble-shooting input files from external sources into CFTC Datawarehouse.
This role ensures the integrity and regulatory value of the Commission's market data by supporting mission-critical reporting and strengthening data quality across both traditional derivatives and rapidly evolving prediction-market ecosystems.

*Must be local the DMV area or Chicago, IL area ONLY.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

Minimum of 8 years with BS/BA; Minimum of 6 years with MS/MA; Minimum of 10 years with an AS/AA; or 12 years with a HS diploma/equivalent
Strong understanding of derivatives markets, including futures, options, swaps, and exchange operations.
Experience/Knowledge of XML, FIXML, FPML
Experience in multi-data-center or cloud environments, including AWS and Redshift tools.
Ability to create detailed technical documentation, mapping specifications, and validation rules.
Excellent communication skills for coordinating with internal teams, external exchanges, and stakeholders.
At least one (1) year of experience using:
SQL, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft Azure, SQL Server Management Studio.
AWS, Redshift, Python

Must be able to go onsite at least 3 days a week.
Must be a US Citizen or a Green Card Holder
Must be able to obtain and maintain a Public Trust Clearance

Preferred Qualifications:

Active Public Trust Clearance is a plus
SQL querying skills, AWS tools skills
Financial Industry Certifications is a plus
Prior experience with prediction-market data or familiarity with how these markets operate is a plus.
Experience with SAS, data visualization using programming languages, (e.g. Python or R), or commercial tools (e.g. MicroStrategy, Tableau) (Preferred, not required)

Details

Target Salary Range: $86,000 - $138,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual's experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

Benefits Statement: Peraton offers eligible employees a variety of benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, health savings account, short/long term disability, EAP, parental leave, 401(k), paid time off (PTO) for vacation, and company paid holidays. A full listing of available benefits can be viewed at https://www.careers.peraton.com/benefits.

Application Statements: The application period for the job is estimated to be 30 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. By applying to this job, you are expressing interest in the role and the Company. During the review of your application, you may be required to participate in an on-camera interview, as well as participate in a process to verify your identity. Use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools of any kind during Peraton interviews is strictly prohibited unless the candidate has obtained prior written authorization. All interview responses must be the candidate's own.

EEO:
Equal opportunity employer, including disability and protected veterans, or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.description:
Description

MUST HAVES:

ServiceNow Business Analyst

ITSM

Service Management

AI Projects - Now Assist, Virtual Agent, Control Tower, Copilot, Chatgpt, Claud, etc.

Position Overview

Position Overview

We are seeking a Senior ServiceNow AI Business Analyst to support a large-scale ServiceNow AI Service Management transformation. This individual will work closely with business stakeholders, ServiceNow product owners, architects, developers, process owners, and AI teams to identify, define, and translate business needs into well-structured AI-enabled ServiceNow use cases and requirements.

The ideal candidate brings a strong foundation in ServiceNow ITSM and Business Analysis, combined with hands-on knowledge of ServiceNow AI capabilities, particularly Now Assist.

This is not a traditional requirements-gathering BA role. The successful candidate must be comfortable challenging and refining stakeholder requests, understanding where AI adds value and where it does not, and asking the deeper questions necessary to turn an AI idea into a solution that can be designed, configured, tested, governed, and measured.

Responsibilities

AI Use-Case Discovery & Requirements

Lead discovery sessions and requirements workshops with business and technology stakeholders to identify opportunities for AI within ServiceNow.

Translate high-level requests and business problems into clearly structured AI use cases, functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and process flows.

Ask Targeted AI-specific Discovery Questions, Including

What business problem are we trying to solve?

Who will consume or act upon the AI-generated output?

What information or knowledge should the AI use?

What decisions can the AI assist with versus make or execute?

Where is human review or approval required?

What constitutes an acceptable AI response?

What should happen when the AI is uncertain, incorrect, or unable to answer?

What data, privacy, security, or access restrictions apply?

How will we measure whether the AI capability is actually delivering value?

Evaluate requests for feasibility, business value, user impact, dependencies, risks, and readiness.

Skills

Business analysis, AI, Servicenow, Agile, Requirements gathering, Business requirements, ITSM, Requirement gathering, User stories

Top Skills Details

Business analysis,AI,Servicenow,Agile,Requirements gathering,Business requirements,ITSM,Requirement gathering

Additional Skills & Qualifications

5+ years of experience as a Business Analyst, Senior Business Analyst, Product Analyst, or similar role supporting enterprise technology initiatives.

Strong hands-on experience working within the ServiceNow ecosystem.

Strong understanding of ServiceNow ITSM, including Incident, Problem, Change, Request, Knowledge Management and Service Catalog processes.

Experience supporting ServiceNow AI, Now Assist, Virtual Agent, AI Search, Predictive Intelligence, Generative AI, or comparable AI-enabled ServiceNow initiatives.

Demonstrated ability to facilitate complex stakeholder discovery and requirements workshops.

Strong Experience Converting Business Needs Into

User stories

Functional requirements

Acceptance criteria

Process/workflow diagrams

Use cases

Backlog items

Understanding of Generative AI and enterprise AI concepts, particularly the considerations that differ from traditional workflow automation.

Ability to work effectively with Product Owners, ServiceNow Architects, Developers, ITSM process owners, data teams and business stakeholders.

Experience Level

Expert Leve

Job Type & Location

This is a Contract position based out of Washington D.C., DC.

Pay And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $65.00 - $75.00/hr.

Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors.

Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to specific elections, plan, or program terms. If eligible, the benefits available for this temporary role may include the following: Medical, dental & vision Critical Illness, Accident, and Hospital 401(k) Retirement Plan Pre-tax and Roth post-tax contributions available Life Insurance (Voluntary Life & AD&D for the employee and dependents) Short and long-term disability Health Spending Account (HSA) Transportation benefits Employee Assistance Program Time Off/Leave (PTO, Vacation or Sick Leave)

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
About The Company

Medline is a growing, worldwide organization committed to supporting healthcare and the people and communities it serves. The company offers employees opportunities to develop their skills, continue their education, and build careers across a broad organization. Medline is dedicated to fostering a workplace where people feel they belong and have the tools and resources to perform at their best. Through a focus on inclusion, professional growth, and continuous improvement, Medline aims to help employees contribute meaningfully while advancing their careers.

About The Role

Medline is seeking a Project Manager to lead the end-to-end delivery of small- to medium-scale projects. Under moderate supervision, you will guide projects from planning through completion, ensuring objectives are clearly defined and deliverables are achieved on time, within scope, and within budget. You will partner with cross-functional teams and stakeholders to keep work aligned with business priorities, address challenges, and maintain momentum. This role is well suited to a collaborative, organized professional who can manage competing priorities, communicate clearly, and bring structure to projects with meaningful visibility and stakeholder complexity.

Qualifications

A bachelor’s degree in a related field is required, along with two to four years of project management experience. Candidates should have demonstrated experience leading projects involving elevated risk, visibility, or stakeholder complexity. A strong understanding of project management methodologies, tools, and governance practices is important, as is the ability to apply them to project planning, execution, monitoring, and reporting.

The successful candidate will be organized, analytical, and comfortable managing multiple priorities. Strong communication and problem-solving skills are essential, along with the ability to coordinate across functions and influence stakeholders at different levels of an organization. A Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is preferred.

Responsibilities

Lead the full project lifecycle for assigned small- to medium-scale initiatives, establishing objectives and guiding teams toward agreed outcomes. Develop detailed project plans that define scope, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, and timelines. Coordinate resources and manage project budgets, monitoring progress and taking appropriate action to keep work on track.

Identify potential risks and issues early, develop mitigation approaches, and resolve challenges where possible. Escalate concerns when needed to support timely decisions and protect project objectives. Track key performance indicators and provide stakeholders with clear, accurate updates on status, risks, decisions, and outcomes. Facilitate project meetings, encourage effective cross-functional coordination, and maintain consistent communication with team members and stakeholders throughout delivery.

Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to enhance project workflows, templates, tools, and governance practices. Share recommendations that help teams plan and deliver work more consistently and effectively.

Benefits

Medline Industries, LP, and its subsidiaries offer a competitive total rewards package, continuing education and training, and potential for career growth within a worldwide organization. The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $79,000 to $119,000. Actual compensation may vary based on location, education, experience, skills, and abilities. This role may be eligible for bonus and/or incentive compensation. Medline will not pay less than the applicable minimum wage or salary threshold.

For employees working an average of 30 or more hours per week, benefits include health insurance, life and disability coverage, 401(k) contributions, and paid time off. Employees working fewer than 30 hours per week may have access to 401(k) contributions, paid time off, the Employee Assistance Program, Employee Resource Groups, and the Employee Service Corp. Benefit eligibility and details are subject to applicable plan terms.

Equal Opportunity

Medline Industries, LP is an equal opportunity employer. Medline evaluates qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, neurodivergence, protected veteran status, marital or family status, caregiver responsibilities, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. Medline is committed to seeking diversity in all forms, acting inclusively, and creating an environment where everyone can belong and grow their career.

jobs.description:
For questions regarding this position, please contact the Recruiter listed in the Supplemental Information section.

About The Position

Riverside University Health System (RUHS) seeks candidates for an RUHS Compliance Program Manager position. This role supports the development, coordination, implementation, and oversight of RUHS corporate compliance programs and activities. The selected candidate will supervise support staff, ensure adherence to applicable regulations, and perform related duties as required. Current certification in Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC)
is strongly preferred.

Key Responsibilities Include

Supporting compliance with federal, state, and county laws and regulations, including HITECH.
Providing subject matter expertise on medical privacy and information security.
Overseeing staff and managing program activities as assigned.
Assisting in achieving compliance goals and strategic objectives.

The RUHS Compliance Program Manager is a journey-level manager classification reporting to the RUHS/County Compliance and Privacy Officer. Incumbents are expected to perform complex and increasingly responsible work with minimal supervision, contributing to the design, execution, and monitoring of effective compliance programs. This position is distinct from the RUHS/County Compliance and Privacy Officer, which entails broader responsibilities in directing and managing regulatory compliance programs.

This class has been deemed eligible for the Performance Recognition Plan as set forth under Article 3, Section 311(C) of the County Management Resolution. Program eligibility requires employees to be in a leadership position, manage other employees or programs, and have significant influence on the achievement of organizational objectives.

Why RUHS Medical Center?

Riverside University Health System-Medical Center is nationally recognized for its innovative, progressive care and is considered one of the top employers in the region. The 439-bed Medical Center is a designated Stroke Center, Level I Trauma Center, and home to the only Pediatric ICU in the area.

For more information about RUHS Medical Center, please visit ruhealth.org .

Examples Of Essential Duties

Perform audits to assess compliance with various laws, regulations, policies, and standards such as those related to healthcare fraud, waste and abuse, billing and coding, clinical documentation, privacy and information security, research and ethics; maintain a system of reporting that provides timely and relevant information of all aspects of compliance issues.
Participate in appropriate level of response, develop corrective action plans and conduct compliance investigations while maintaining confidentiality of information reported, as appropriate.
Evaluate departmental continuous readiness to achieve compliance in the areas of healthcare privacy and security; assist in the development and implementation of privacy policies, procedures and breach notification as necessary.
Develop and implement policies and procedures for filing and investigation of complaints related to HIPAA/HITECH Privacy, Breach Notification Rules and related County guidelines and procedures.
Develop and monitor policies and procedures that establish standards for ensuring patient privacy protections, including by providing guidance to individual employees and departments on the HIPAA Privacy Rule, as appropriate.
Document and retain all complaints received as required by HIPAA/HITECH; establish and maintain a mechanism for tracking and reporting the investigation and resolving such complaints.
Develop and administer training for RUHS staff to promote awareness of compliance to regulatory standards.
Provide guidance and assistance to departments on a variety of privacy and compliance auditing, and internal control matters; document findings and prepare reports.
Supervise, assign, review, and evaluate the work performed by staff; direct the day-to-day operations of support staff.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree, preferably with a major in business administration, public administration, public health nursing, finance, accounting, or a closely related field to the assignment. (A master's degree from an accredited college or university in any of the aforementioned majors is preferred.) Possession of current Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC) certification is preferred.

Experience:
Three years of professional, journey-level experience in healthcare compliance, which includes internal auditing experience and experience in the development and implementation of HIPAA and/or privacy compliance programs.

Knowledge of:
Information security; theory, principles and practices of general healthcare; governmental accounting, budgeting and auditing; HIPAA privacy and security rules and regulations; privacy laws, rules and regulations relating to information and security; federal, state and local codes, rules and regulations including healthcare fiscal operations; the methods of developing systems forms for various types of accounting records and reports; information systems and their application to accounting operations; the principles, methods and techniques of public administration, personnel and business office management; the principles and techniques of supervision.

Ability to:
Develop and implement compliance and auditing programs; apply legal and administrative compliance policies to hospital or health systems; analyze data, draw logical conclusions, conduct independent audits, reviews, and make evaluations to ensure compliance issues and concerns are appropriately evaluated, investigated and resolved; recommend effective courses of action; communicate effectively in oral and written form; establish and maintain effective working relationships; conduct independent systems analyses of complex business processes.

jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure
using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite
, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California
, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Safety
jobs.description:
Join the team bringing advanced autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

This is Bedrock's first dedicated Safety Technical Program Manager
, a role built to establish the execution structure that lets us roll out new autonomy capabilities quickly without compromising safety rigor. As we scale to new machine types and expanded operational domains, we are evolving our safety practices toward more explicit, strategic execution.

You will own program execution for the safety, systems engineering, and state estimation work that makes autonomous heavy equipment safe to operate in the real world. This is a hands-on individual contributor role driving alignment and delivery across engineering, safety, autonomy, hardware, and field operations through influence, structure, and clear communication. You will be the connective tissue between safety strategy and technical delivery, making sure requirements are traceable, dependencies are visible, and risks surface early enough to act on. We are a startup that values agility. We believe that speed and safety are compatible when the traceability behind them is solid.

What You'll Do

Own planning and strategic execution for the safety and systems portions of the autonomy roadmap, from requirements through validated field deployment.
Support safety requirements being traceable, reusable across platforms and sites, and integrated into roadmaps from inception, partnering with safety and systems engineering on hazard analysis, validation evidence, and release readiness.
Build and maintain the validation plan spanning simulation and on-site testing, ensuring system-level changes are verified before they reach customers.
Map and actively manage dependencies and tradeoffs across systems, hardware, software, state estimation, and safety, weighing safety impact alongside schedule impact and identifying single points of failure on the critical path before they slip.
Drive program reviews, risk, and change management for multi-disciplinary, safety-critical initiatives, and provide reporting on roadmap health, delivery status, and safety implications clear enough to support both executive decisions and customer-facing discussions.
Translate field signals into prioritized engineering work and tracking issues to resolution.

What You'll Bring

7+ years of technical program management experience, including 2+ years leading programs involving safety-critical or high-integrity systems.
Domain experience in robotics, autonomous systems, aerospace, or another physical-world safety-critical domain, with a working understanding of the software, firmware, and hardware stacks behind real-world autonomy.
Working familiarity with a functional safety standard, such as ISO 26262 or IEC 61508, and how it shapes program structure, evidence, and release gates.
Enough working fluency in statistics and probability to interpret validation results and reliability metrics critically, not just track that they exist.
Understanding of the rigor, validation, and cross-functional coordination required to operate reliably in the physical world.
A track record of managing complex, cross-functional programs under ambiguity, taking systems from concept to production.
The ability to operate at a deep technical level and to distill complex risks and interdependencies into aligned, actionable plans for engineers and executives alike.
Strong dependency, risk, and change-management instincts in environments where safety and schedule are both non-negotiable.
A track record of thriving in fast-paced, high-ownership environments, with startup experience strongly preferred and a bias toward building structure that helps us scale through complexity.
Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.

The incumbent must possess the technical acumen to design/analyze/assess program details, have proficiency in financial or economic analysis to optimize results and recommend adjustment to program initiatives, all to achieve defined improvement results.

The position requires excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to lead the preparation of complex reports and presentations. This level will frequently interface with all levels of management including GMs, VPs, Senior VPs, and the senior management groups.

The position requires a high level of coordination skills as well as the ability to manage complex technical projects involving other departments, outside consultants and industry groups. The Program Manager is expected to frequently interface with industry groups and peers to benchmark best practices and to lead the industry in a rapidly changing environment.

Identify opportunities for multi-year vendor relationships to leverage cost savings and bundling opportunities. Assist with the resolution of contract performance commercial issues when stalled at the project level.
Develop and lead routine program assessment activities to provide early identification of gaps and program issues. Provide support for RRE stations during audits, assessments, and outage preparation and execution activities. Create tools and templates to perform gap analysis on important programmatic areas and prioritize recommendations that will lead to improvement action plans.
Influence business unit leaders on implementation of consistent standards across the business unit. Lead industry peer groups to ensure company engagement with emerging issues. Actively integrates industry best practices into Duke Energy fleet initiatives and programs. Establish metrics and KPIs in support of fleet initiatives and business targets. Revise initiatives to respond to changing industry/fleet trends and priorities

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Works with management and stakeholders to align priorities and goals using technical know-how in a fundamental engineering area or technical domain. Establishes scope and milestones for each aspect of a technical program, aligning to the broader program plan and company strategies and goals. Manages technical programs and complex, cross-organizational initiatives impacting products and business. Manages highly complex issues, bottlenecks and/or risks, escalating issues when appropriate. Leads technical program improvement, implementing best practices and driving cross-team process optimizations to improve processes. Leads efforts to integrate continuous improvement within technical programs, driving insights across many workstreams to generate recommendations that deliver operational efficiencies. Facilitates collaboration across multiple teams, driving technical discussions that align priorities and program goals. Provides technical expertise, direction and mentorship to cross-functional teams. Creates and automates reporting, partnering with development teams to continue improving reports, dashboards, forecasts, and models to help manage technical program execution. Acts as a technical liaison with or between stakeholder teams, driving effective collaboration for customer success within Oracle commitments.

Responsibilities

Technical Management and Execution - Technical Management:

– Leverages technical knowledge to identify risks, manage scope, estimate program timelines, request feasibility, testing requirements, and determine appropriate resources.

– Forecasts program demands and resourcing to identify risks and ensure that goals are achievable.

– Leads the development and implementation of evolving processes to ensure that organizational SLAs are met.

Technical Management and Execution - Technical Strategy and Execution:

– Utilizes technical knowledge to identify, track, and manage program dependencies and risks.

– Supports rapid response to escalations, coordinating within team and communicating to senior team members to assess risk, determine mitigation strategies, and execute the optimal proposed path to resolution.

– Supports planning by identifying dependencies and risks.

– Develops delivery standards and guidelines in alignment with Oracle best practices.

– Identifies and quantifies opportunities for process automations and advocates for prioritization.

– Contributes to incident management efforts and identifies opportunities to improve processes, as applicable.

Program Oversight - Strategy and Decision-Making:

– Aligns priorities with customers, service, and stakeholder teams through regular reporting to senior leadership.

– Establishes scope and milestones for each program, aligning to the broader program plan and company strategies and goals.

– Assists in defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and measurement methods for program performance against established goals (e.g., scope, timelines, deliverable quality).

– Builds, maintains, and executes a clear communication strategy of objectives to partners and customers, influencing decision-making regarding best practices for Oracle systems.

Program Oversight - Program and Operations Management:

– Manages both technical and non-technical programs and complex, cross-organizational programs impacting products and business.

– Maintains comprehensive program documentation (e.g., status reports, program plans) and documents risks and issues.

– Ensures attention to detail in program management from planning to execution and reporting.

– Leads regular program status meetings and keeps teams and leadership informed.

– Leads initiatives within the team to improve operational efficiency and enhance adherence to service level agreements (SLAs) and productivity targets.

– Ensures ownership and accountability for forecasting program demands, funding, and resourcing.

– Guides the deployment of change management for programs, such as priority, scope, scheduling, or requirement changes.

Program Oversight - Risk Management:

– Manages highly complex issues, bottlenecks and/or risks, escalating issues when appropriate.

– Conducts comprehensive assessments of costs, benefits, and return on investment (ROI) to inform decision-making and risk mitigation strategies.

– Manages critical issues while making trade-offs between business needs and technical constraints.

– Removes blockers for the program and identifies new technical and resource options to efficiently deliver solutions and drive adoption.

Process Efficiency - Process Optimization:

– Leads program improvement, implementing best practices and driving cross-team process optimizations to improve processes.

– Organizes and develops program objectives and workflows, while testing and deploying cross-functional solutions to address critical business problems.

– Collaborates with management to initiate and maintain processes and procedures that guide and assist teams in reaching their goals.

Process Efficiency - Continuous Improvement:

– Leads efforts to integrate continuous improvement within programs, driving insights across many workstreams to generate recommendations that deliver operational efficiencies.

– Develops and standardizes data-driven decision-making frameworks, ensuring insights drive efficiencies.

– Identifies and addresses gaps to facilitate business-critical improvements to the solution's availability and reliability.

– Iterates processes based on feedback and KPIs, analyzing results through retrospectives.

– Defines requirements and configurations of existing and new development tools, where applicable.

Collaboration and Program Leadership - Cross Functional Collaboration:

– Facilitates collaboration across multiple teams, driving discussions that align priorities and program goals.

– Leads medium-scale efforts to optimize processes, identifying and implementing solutions that enhance team efficiency.

– Delivers program updates, risks, and opportunities to managers and leadership, influencing decision-making.

– Develops relationships with key stakeholders, ensuring their perspectives are integrated into program planning and execution.

Collaboration and Program Leadership - Program Leadership:

– Leads programs to continuously improve organizational efficiency.

– Provides technical direction and mentorship to cross-functional teams.

– Influences and guides change at all levels of the group from initiation through delivery.

– Ensures that the program team and other stakeholders are aligned with the program goals and motivated, identifying and addressing conflicts and issues.

Data and Analysis:

– Creates and automates reporting, partnering with development teams to continue improving reports, dashboards, forecasts, and models to help manage program execution.

– Conducts analysis on a small number of data sources with moderate complexity, which may include competitive analysis, trend analysis, and KPI analysis, to drive data-informed decisions to support the program goals, presenting findings with immediate teams stakeholders.

Stakeholder Engagement:

– Acts as a liaison with or between stakeholder teams, driving effective collaboration for customer success within Oracle commitments.

– Manages relationships with internal and external stakeholders to align program priorities and commitments.

– Identifies and documents stakeholder needs and works cross-functionally to implement solutions that enhance satisfaction.

– Identifies risks to customer satisfaction and advocates for improvements or mitigation.

– Assesses risks to customer satisfaction and evaluates mitigation efforts, providing solutions to the immediate team and related teams to ensure alignment on resolving these risks.

– Helps balance team priorities and Oracle commitments to ensure optimal coverage and response to key customer needs, minimizing risks to the program.

Planning & Execution:

Efficiently delegates, monitors, and prioritizes work across multiple projects, providing technical oversight and adjusting plans to address shifts in resources or timelines.

Leverages understanding of business leaders, stakeholders, and/or customers to ensure proposed solutions meet their needs. Supports inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.

Problem Solving:

Continuous Learning:

Proactively seeks and leverages ongoing feedback and training to improve skills. Coaches and mentors junior team members, fostering continuous learning and knowledge sharing within and across teams.

Solicits feedback from others on ideas for alternative approaches and methods for continued improvement.

Only Oracle brings together the data, infrastructure, applications, and expertise to power everything from industry innovations to life-saving care. And with AI embedded across our products and services, we help customers turn that promise into a better future for all. Discover your potential at a company leading the way in AI and cloud solutions that impact billions of lives.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Program Manager
jobs.description:
Responsibilities

MaxLinear is seeking a high energy and experienced Senior Engineering Program Manager for this high-visibility role leading the full project lifecycle of engineering R&D programs including planning, tracking, and execution. In this role, you will focus on:

Lead planning, tracking, and execution of R&D programs at corporate headquarters through close collaboration with cross-functional engineering leads and senior management
Develop detailed staffing plan and bottom-up schedule for R&D programs that involve RF/AMS, DSP algorithms, SOC, Software, System and System Integration and Test teams
Establish program Plan of Record and success metrics and track continuously
Manage program execution to ensure product leadership, while meeting quality, timeline, and cost requirements; manage execution risks by implementing mitigation strategies and contingency plans
Report on program status, issues, and action plans to business unit program management and to senior management
Ensure program adherence to MaxLinear’s Process Development Methodology and assure project lifecycle compliance, including reviews and lessons learned sessions, and continuous improvements in processes, cross-functional development flows, and execution excellence
Manage relationships with all program stakeholders, suppliers, and customers to optimize outcomes

Qualifications

Knowledge and broad experience across technical disciplines including: RF/AMS, DSP, SoC, Systems, Software, and System Integration and Test
Deep expertise in one or more of these areas:
Track record of hands-on technical program / project management or engineering chip lead experience over multiple product cycles
In-depth understanding of engineering workflows, validation methodologies, and processes
Exposure to chip bring up, debug, system integration and lab validation

Creative problem solver with execution mindset, ability to excel and lead cross-functional technical teams to deliver to plans of record
Self-motivated with excellent communication skills
BS + 11 years of experience, MS + 9 years of experience or equivalent, or Ph.D. + 6 years of experience

Compensation And Benefits

MaxLinear has a Total Compensation philosophy which includes base salary and annual discretionary bonus eligibility and many positions also include stock-based compensation.

MaxLinear's good faith estimate starting base salary range is: $168,000 to $208,000 Annually

We offer competitive benefits designed to support employee health, welfare, and retirement and some highlights are: health care benefits, 401k savings plan, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), and paid time off.

The actual starting base salary will be determined by the match to certain role-related criteria such as educational degree(s) or equivalent, relevant work experience, skillset needed for the role, and geographic location; this is not an all-inclusive list as some roles may require unique skills or experience.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, and will not be discriminated against based on race, sex, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status.

Company Overview

MaxLinear is a global, NASDAQ-traded company (MXL) where the entrepreneurial spirit is alive and well. We are a fabless system-on-chip product company, striving to improve the world’s communication networks for everyone through our highly integrated radio-frequency (RF), analog, digital, and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions for access and connectivity, wired and wireless infrastructure, and industrial and multi-market applications.

We hire the best people in the industry and engage them in some of the most exciting opportunities that connect the world we live in today. Our growth has come from innovative, bold approaches to solving some of the world’s most challenging communication technology problems in the most efficient and effective manner.

MaxLinear began by developing the world’s first high-performance TV tuner chip using standard CMOS process technology. Others said we couldn’t achieve the extremely high-performance requirements using CMOS, but we proved them wrong and achieved enduring global market leadership with our designs. Since then, we’ve developed a full line of products that drive 4G and 5G infrastructure; enable data center, metro and long-haul optical interconnects; bring 10Gbit to the home; power the IoT revolution; and enable robust and reliable communication in harsh industrial environments. Over the years, we’ve expanded through organic growth and through several acquisitions that have perfectly complemented our existing portfolio and enabled us to deliver complete end-to-end solutions in our target markets. One such example was the acquisition of Intel’s Home Gateway Platform Division that added Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and Broadband Gateway Processor SoC technology to our connected home portfolio creating a complete and scalable platform of connectivity and access solutions to fully address our customers’ needs.

Our headquarters are in Carlsbad, near San Diego, California. We also have major design centers in Irvine and San Jose, California; Valencia, Spain; Bangalore, India; Munich, Germany; Israel; and Singapore.

We have approximately 1,200 employees, a substantial majority of whom have engineering degrees and include masters and Ph.D. graduates from many of the premiere universities around the world. Our employees thrive on innovation, outstanding execution, outside-the-box thinking, nimbleness, and collaboration. Together, we form a high-energy business team that is focused on building the best and most innovative products on the market.

Who We Are

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About The Team

Equipment Monitoring (EM) is Motive's connected-asset product line, covering asset gateways, beacons, and environmental and door sensors. EM is one of Motive's high-growth business lines, and we have an ambitious roadmap to execute. The EM team owns the end-to-end customer experience, from the device to the cloud, web, and mobile software customers use every day.

About The Role

As the Cloud Software TPM for Equipment Monitoring, you will own the end-to-end delivery of EM programs across cloud software (backend, frontend, and mobile), from quarterly planning and sprint execution through customer launch and adoption. Most EM projects combine embedded, IoT, backend, and frontend work, and you will make sure those pieces come together into one cohesive plan with clear owners, milestones, and dependencies.

You will be accountable for the customer deliverables, release readiness, and measurable business outcomes of each program. Where a program involves hardware, firmware, or embedded work, you will partner closely with the hardware org TPM and embedded counterparts to work out dependencies and stay in sync on timelines and readiness, while driving the overall plan through to launch. Your ownership and delivery directly shape EM's impact on customers.

What You'll Do

Plan: Partner with EM Product and Engineering to turn quarterly and half-year roadmaps into detailed cloud software project plans with milestones, owners, measurable customer and business outcomes, and risks.
Connect the pieces: Track cross-team dependencies for each project across embedded, hardware, IoT/Platform, Product Ops, PMM, Design, and Support, partnering closely with the hardware org TPM on devices and international rollouts so projects don't stall in the gaps between teams and customer commitments are met.
Own end-to-end delivery: Be accountable for each program from kickoff through customer launch and adoption, tracking milestones across concurrent programs, surfacing risks and tradeoffs early (scope, quality, and timeline), and driving decisions with stakeholders and leadership to keep delivery on track. Use customer feedback and support signals to close the loop after launch.
Communicate: Maintain a single source of truth for program status, share weekly updates, and report program health, risks, and outcomes in monthly and quarterly business reviews, translating technical detail into business impact.
Run the operating rhythm: Facilitate sprint planning, backlog grooming, retrospectives, and demos for EM cloud engineering, and drive release-readiness checkpoints so quality risks surface before launch.
Improve how we work: Run intake and triage for ad-hoc requests, fix recurring execution gaps with durable solutions, and lead quarter- and project-level retrospectives.

What We're Looking For

5+ years of experience in technical program management, with the technical fluency to engage credibly with engineers on architecture, tradeoffs, and delivery risks; a technical degree or equivalent experience is recommended.
Proven track record leading large, ambiguous, multi-team cloud software programs (backend, web, mobile) with significant cross-team dependencies and measurable customer or business impact.
Bias for action and root-cause problem solving over administrative tracking.
Strong organization and communication; ability to lead and coach without authority across distributed teams and to translate technical detail into clear updates for leadership.
Ability to define and track quality and delivery metrics (for example, escaped defects, reliability, predictability, customer feedback) and turn data into an action plan.
Comfort in a fast-paced, changing environment, building process where little exists.
Experience with Jira, Confluence, or similar tools, strong knowledge of agile methods, and experience using automation (including AI tools) to keep programs visible without manual overhead for engineers.

Preferred Experience

Exposure to connected-device or IoT products (firmware release cycles, device qualification, OTA updates), which helps in partnering with hardware and embedded teams.
CSM or PMP certification.

Pay Transparency

Your compensation may be based on several factors, including education, work experience, and certifications. For certain roles, total compensation may include restricted stock units. Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Learn more about our benefits by visiting Motive Perks & Benefits.

Job Description

Every transaction tells a story. Every innovation creates new possibilities. At FIS, we build the technology that helps businesses and communities thrive. Join us and be part of a team that embraces curiosity, values diverse perspectives and turns ideas into action.

About The Role

As a Project Manager Lead within Technology Development Enablement, you will provide strategic direction and delivery leadership for large, multifaceted technology initiatives. You will guide cross-functional teams through planning, execution, monitoring and closeout while aligning scope, schedules, costs, resources, risks and dependencies with organizational objectives. This role requires strong autonomy, sound judgment and the ability to turn complex information into clear decisions, commitments and executive-level communication.

Your Key Responsibilities

Lead large-scale technology enablement programs, data migrations, and projects from initiation through closeout, establishing clear outcomes, scope, governance, plans, milestones, resources and success measures
Develop and maintain integrated delivery plans that coordinate schedules, costs, dependencies, risks, issues, assumptions and decisions across multiple workstreams and stakeholder groups
Direct execution, monitor performance and implement corrective actions to keep deliverables aligned with agreed timelines, financial parameters, quality standards and business objectives
Analyze complex technical project information and data to identify trends, constraints and delivery risks, then provide actionable recommendations that support timely leadership decisions
Facilitate cross-functional alignment among business, product, engineering, operations, finance, risk, security, vendors and other partners, resolving trade-offs and escalating decisions when needed
Build implementation readiness through stakeholder engagement, communications, training, adoption planning and transition-to-operations activities, with measurable follow-through after launch
Establish fit-for-purpose governance, reporting and quality-control mechanisms that provide transparent status, decision logs and evidence of delivery performance
Provide expert guidance, mentoring and practical support to project team members, strengthening project-management practices and the team’s ability to deliver complex work

What You Bring

Required qualifications

Extensive project or program management experience leading large-scale, cross-functional technology initiatives with significant organizational impact
Demonstrated skill integrating scope, schedule, cost, resources, risks, dependencies, quality and stakeholder commitments into an executable delivery plan
Experience leading projects in financial technology, banking, payments, capital markets or another highly regulated and operationally complex environment
Strong analytical and decision-support skills, including the ability to navigate complex data, assess feasibility and recommend actions that improve delivery outcomes
Excellent executive communication, facilitation and stakeholder-management skills, with experience gaining cooperation across internal teams, clients, vendors and external partners
Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy, determine appropriate methods for new assignments and lead teams through ambiguous or challenging situations
A university degree in business, technology, project management or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and relevant experience

Preferred Qualifications

Project management certification such as Project Management Professional (PMP), Program Management Professional (PgMP) or an agile delivery credential
Experience with enterprise delivery and portfolio tools such as Jira, Aha! or Planview; and executive status reporting, RAID management and dependency tracking
Experience leading enterprise tooling, process-governance, reporting, data, controls or technology-adoption initiatives

The impact you’ll make

As a Project Manager Lead, you will create the structure and alignment needed to move strategic technology initiatives from intent to measurable outcomes. Your leadership will make scope, dependencies, risks and decisions visible, help teams coordinate effectively and strengthen delivery reliability. Through disciplined planning, transparent governance and strong stakeholder partnerships, you will help Technology Development Enablement scale platforms, processes and ways of working across the enterprise.

When you join FIS, you become part of a team that's shaping how the world pays, banks and invests. We’re committed to helping you thrive, both professionally and personally. At FIS, we offer you~

jobs.description:
Location

Atlanta, GA (In-Person, In-Office)

Job Summary

Georgia Tech's Office of Information Technology (OIT) is seeking a seasoned program manager with Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) expertise to oversee CMMC-compliant onboarding of researchers and laboratories to the Institute's Shield secure research service and operational support to their Shield-based work. Shield supports research activities involving controlled unclassified information (CUI) that Georgia Tech conducts on behalf of the Department of War (DOW) and other U.S. Government sponsors. GT Shield is certified at CMMC Level 2 following a third-party (C3PAO) assessment, meeting all NIST SP 800-171 requirements.

Job Summary

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to shape the expansion of Shield to the Georgia Tech research enterprise, including laboratory environments that conduct cutting-edge research on a broad range of topics.

The successful candidate will bring deep experience with CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, and building, transforming, or materially improving programs operating in complex regulated environments and will be expected to operate as a trusted advisor to cybersecurity leadership and institutional stakeholders.

This position offers a unique opportunity to shape the trajectory of CMMC-compliant research at one of the worlds leading research universities. The role provides broad visibility across the Institute's research enterprise, significant autonomy, and the ability to shape and expand CMMC-compliant research practices at Georgia Tech.

Georgia Tech is a top-ranked public research university situated in the heart of Atlanta, a diverse and vibrant city with significant economic and cultural strengths. The Institute serves more than 45,000 students through top-ranked undergraduate, graduate, and executive programs in engineering, computing, science, business, design, and liberal arts. Georgia Tech's faculty attracted more than $1.4 billion in research awards this past year in fields ranging from biomedical technology to artificial intelligence, energy, sustainability, semiconductors, neuroscience, and national security. Georgia Tech ranks among the nation¿s top 20 universities for research and development spending and No. 1 among institutions without a medical school.

Job Duty 1 -

Lead project teams through planning, assigning and overseeing diverse activities; define project goals, objectives, scope and estimates of schedules, resources and costs involving multiple projects being conducted simultaneously.

Job Duty 2 -

Direct project execution through continual coordination of planning, tasking, performance reporting, change control and issue management.

Job Duty 3 -

Confer with functional users within an assigned business or service area to develop plans to address business needs; develop and implement change management strategies.

Job Duty 4 -

Initiate communications among project teams, customers and appropriate levels of management.

Job Duty 5 -

Deliver project status reports and presentations.

Job Duty 6 -

About Us

Custom Fireplace Patio & BBQ is an outdoor living store based in Pleasanton, Ca. We have been in the industry since 1972, specializing in high end outdoor kitchens, fireplaces, and everything outdoor.

The Role

We're hiring a Field Project Manager to lead our installation team and own the technical side of the installations. You'll manage and support our field techs day to day, and when techs, contractors, or our sales people need answers, you're the person they call. You'll be based in our Pleasanton office and visit job sites from San Jose to Napa.

What You'll Do

• Manage and support our installation and service technicians
• Perform site visits before install to measure, assess conditions, and flag anything that affects the quote
• Make sure every install meets manufacturer specs, clearances, and requirements
• Review plans, shop drawings, and submittals
• Coordinate with homeowners, contractors, designers, and architects so sites are ready on install day

What You Bring

• Experience managing multi-trade installation projects
• Comfort reading plans, submittals, and shop drawings
• Clear, confident communication with customers and crews

A mix of office and field work. You must be able to climb ladders, lift up to 50 lbs, access rooftops and confined spaces, and work outdoors in all weather.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Bamboo Health is the leader in Real-Time Care Intelligence™ solutions aimed at improving lives for everyone experiencing physical and behavioral health challenges. We are driven by our mission to empower clients to deliver seamless, high-quality and cost-effective care during pivotal moments to improve health outcomes. From coast to coast, Bamboo Health partners with all major retail pharmacy chains, 52 states and territories, 100% of the top 10 best hospitals and more than half of the country’s largest health plans to improve more than 1 billion patient encounters annually. Join us in improving lives during pivotal care moments!

Summary

Bamboo Health is building a team of compassionate clinicians and leaders who are committed to improving care access to those in most need. We are seeking a seasoned, highly motivated Senior Project Manager who can bridge clinical, operational, and technical workstreams across provider and payor organizations. This role owns end-to-end project delivery—from initial scoping through go-live and post-launch stabilization—while consulting directly with customers on workflow design to drive results and accelerate implementation timelines. In addition to leading individual implementations, you will manage a portfolio of partner engagements, balancing competing priorities, risks, and stakeholder needs while helping scale implementation best practices across the organization. The ideal candidate brings a strong mix of project management and client success experience, deep healthcare delivery knowledge, and the judgment to work independently with minimal oversight, comfortably tailoring communication across a variety of stakeholders and cross-functional teams.

What You’ll Do

Own the full implementation lifecycle for new provider or payor partners, working independently and with minimal oversight to ensure all milestones, deliverables, and outcomes are met on time and within scope.
Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for external partners, including health systems, provider networks, and payors.
Partner with customers and internal clinical and operational teams to design workflows, staffing models, referral pathways, and escalation processes that support successful implementation and accelerate time to value.
Collaborate with data integration and IT teams to enable connectivity with EHRs, care management platforms, and analytics tools.
Guide partners through workflow changes, training, and adoption planning to drive results and ensure smooth go-live transitions.
Maintain project plans and status reports, as well as risks and issues logs.
Tailor communication of progress, dependencies, and mitigation plans across audiences, from junior project managers to executive leadership, both internally and externally.
Capture lessons learned and feedback to refine implementation methodology, mentor less experienced project managers, and accelerate future rollouts.
Manage a portfolio of concurrent implementations, balancing timelines, risks, dependencies, and stakeholder priorities to ensure successful delivery.
Identify repetitive tasks and partner with team leads to implement scalable automation solutions.

What Success Looks Like…

In 3 months…

Take ownership of at least one active implementation, serving as the primary customer contact while maintaining accurate status reporting, risk management, and stakeholder communication.
Build strong relationships with key internal and external stakeholders and identify opportunities to improve workflows, processes, or implementation efficiency.
Identify at least one opportunity in your role to pilot or apply AI or automation (e.g., streamlining a task, summarizing data, generating content).

In 6 months…

Independently manage a portfolio of concurrent implementations, consistently delivering key milestones on time and within scope.
Lead partners through workflow design, operational readiness, training, adoption planning, and go-live execution.
Serve as a trusted advisor to customers while mentoring less experienced project managers and contributing implementation best practices across the team.

In 12 months…

Deliver multiple successful go-lives with measurable post-launch stabilization, such as partner adoption targets met and time to value shortened compared with baseline.
Capture lessons learned across your implementations and contribute at least two lasting improvements to our implementation playbook, templates, or tools.
Be recognized as a go-to leader for complex implementations, influencing customer outcomes, supporting executive-level partner relationships, and helping elevate implementation excellence across the organization.

What You Need

Bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of combined experience in healthcare project management and account/client success, preferably with exposure to behavioral health, care coordination, or population health in technology enabled services.
Proven success independently leading complex implementations or partnerships involving provider organizations, payors, or health IT vendors, with minimal oversight.
Experience with EHR integrations, referral management workflows, or value-based care initiatives strongly preferred.
A consultative, proactive, solutions-oriented mindset with strong attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to navigate ambiguity, solve complex problems, and independently drive projects forward in dynamic environments.
Strongly empathetic with a keen desire to reduce barriers to behavioral health and social services for the underserved.
Ability to convey technical information and tailor communication across a range of audiences and levels, from junior project managers to clinicians, administrators, and C-level executives, exercising strong, independent judgment in what and how to communicate with customers.
PMP (Project Management Professional, PMI) is preferred.
Comfort using or learning AI-supported tools (e.g., ChatGPT, CoPilot, or role-specific tools) to improve daily workflows.
A forward-thinking, curious mindset with an openness to experimenting with new technologies.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with sound judgment and creativity in designing solutions.
Proven ability to thrive in fast-paced, high-growth, and rapidly evolving environments.
Ability to work effectively in a remote-first environment, ensuring high-quality virtual interactions with minimal distractions.
The ability to travel periodically for work.

What You Get

Join one of the most innovative healthcare technology companies in the country.
Have the autonomy to build something with an enthusiastically supportive team.
Learn from working at the highest levels and on the most strategic priorities of the company, including from world class investors and advisors.
Receive competitive compensation, including health, dental, vision and other benefits.

Belonging at Bamboo

We Care. #BambooHealthValuesCare

Every human being has the right to the best possible healthcare. Our Real-Time Care Intelligence™ solutions enable healthcare professionals to see and treat every individual as a whole person by providing the right information, at the right time – regardless of physical, behavioral or social barriers.

We’re a great place to work because we care. We continually seek to learn about our differences and ensure the unique perspectives and contributions of all employees are welcome, valued and celebrated.

Our commitment to making a positive impact starts by recognizing and leveraging our differences, building inclusive teams and cultivating a sense of belonging.

Southern Nuclear

Job Description

PMO Business Intelligence & Project Performance Analyst

This position may be based in Birmingham, Alabama, or at an SNC nuclear plant—Farley, Hatch, or Vogtle.

Job Summary

Southern Nuclear Operating Company (SNC) operates one of the nation's most respected nuclear generating fleets. The Project Management Office (PMO) provides fleet-level governance, project oversight, performance management, and reporting to support informed decision-making across the enterprise.

The PMO Business Intelligence & Project Performance Analyst develops reporting solutions, dashboards, scorecards, and analytics that provide visibility into project and portfolio performance. Partnering with project management, project controls, finance, engineering, information technology, and site leadership, this role improves data reliability, reporting efficiency, and decision quality by defining meaningful performance measures, identifying trends and risks, and translating complex cost, schedule, financial, resource, and strategic investment data into actionable insights.

Job Requirements

Education

Bachelor's degree in Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Finance, or a related discipline is required.
Advanced degree or relevant certification, such as Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst, Certified Analytics Professional, PMP, or PMI-PBA, is preferred.

Experience

At least five years of experience in business intelligence, data analytics, financial analysis, performance reporting, or a related discipline is required.
Experience in project controls or project management, particularly within large-scale project organizations, project portfolios, capital programs, or complex multidisciplinary project environments, is a plus.
Experience developing Power BI dashboards, executive scorecards, data visualizations, KPIs, and automated reporting solutions is required.
Experience analyzing project cost, schedule, forecast, earned value, risk, resource utilization, and portfolio performance data is preferred.
Experience consolidating and validating data from multiple projects, sites, business units, or enterprise systems is preferred.
Experience with Power BI and Microsoft Excel is required. Experience with SharePoint, Primavera P6, SAP, Microsoft Project, SQL, or comparable project reporting and data platforms is a plus.
Experience supporting a PMO, Finance, or enterprise reporting organization is a plus.
Experience in a utility environment, including nuclear, electric generation, transmission, distribution, or related infrastructure, is a plus.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Advanced proficiency with Power BI, including data modeling, DAX, Power Query, report development, and dashboard design.
Advanced Excel skills and working knowledge of data integration, validation, governance, and reporting controls.
Familiarity with project management and project controls concepts, including project lifecycle management, stage-gate processes, governance, portfolio management, budgeting, forecasting, integrated scheduling, change control, risk management, earned value, and performance measurement.
Ability to translate business requirements into clear report specifications, metric definitions, data models, dashboards, and acceptance criteria.
Ability to interpret performance data, identify trends and root causes, and provide actionable recommendations.
Ability to communicate complex analytical findings through clear visualizations, executive narratives, presentations, and performance reviews.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and handle sensitive information appropriately.
Ability to travel among SNC sites and maintain unescorted access to SNC facilities.

Primary Responsibilities

Develop, maintain, and enhance Power BI dashboards, executive scorecards, KPIs, and project performance reports.
Analyze project and portfolio performance across cost, schedule, forecast, risk, resource utilization, earned value, and financial results.
Develop analytical insights and forecasting information that support executive decision-making, portfolio health assessments, and project prioritization.
Validate and reconcile data; document metric logic, data lineage, and business rules; and ensure reporting accuracy and traceability.
Partner with business and technical stakeholders to gather and define reporting requirements, data ownership, validation controls, and acceptance criteria.
Automate reporting processes to reduce manual effort and improve consistency, reliability, and efficiency.
Prepare executive-level reports, presentations, analytical summaries, and recommendations for leadership.
Support PMO governance metrics and reporting for project reviews, portfolio reviews, monthly reporting cycles, organizational performance management, data governance, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Provide guidance and training to report users and promote consistent interpretation of project performance metrics.
Manage reporting solutions through requirements gathering and definition, design, testing, deployment, documentation, user adoption, and ongoing maintenance.
Evaluate emerging analytics, automation, and artificial intelligence capabilities that improve reporting efficiency, data reliability, and project performance visibility.

BEHAVIORAL ATTRIBUTES

Demonstrates Our Values: Safety First, Unquestionable Trust, Superior Performance, and Total Commitment.
Acts with integrity, professionalism, accountability, and a commitment to data quality.
Builds effective relationships, communicates clearly, and collaborates across organizational boundaries.
Demonstrates intellectual curiosity, initiative, adaptability, and a results -oriented mindset.

PLEASE NOTE

This position may require successful completion of applicable SNC training and qualification requirements as a condition of continued employment.

Southern Nuclear
, a subsidiary of Southern Company (NYSE: SO), is a leader among the nation’s nuclear energy facility operators and an innovator in advanced nuclear technologies. Farley Nuclear Plant near Dothan, Ala., the Edwin I. Hatch Nuclear Plant near Baxley, Ga., and the Alvin W. Vogtle Electric Generating Plant near Waynesboro, Ga.

The company recently achieved commercial operation on Vogtle Units 3&4, representing an historic achievement for the nuclear industry and the country. Vogtle Units 3&4 are the first new nuclear units to reach commercial operation and be built in the United States in the last three decades.
